speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent, and I will be evaluating your lower back pain. Can you describe exactly where the pain radiates down your leg, and did this onset happen after a specific injury or heavy lifting?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain radiating down the side of the leg suggests involvement of the L5 nerve root. Do you have any numbness or tingling in that leg, and are you able to lift your big toe against resistance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see. Does the pain worsen when you cough, sneeze, or strain, and have you noticed any weakness in your foot or difficulty walking on your heels?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. I need to rule out serious neurological compromise; do you have any loss of bowel or bladder control, or numbness in the saddle area (groin and inner thighs)?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good, that rules out cauda equina syndrome. I need to perform a physical exam to confirm the nerve involvement; I will now check your straight leg raise test and assess your reflexes. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_MRI
